concepts.title: Psychology as the Science of Mind and Behaviour
concepts.definition: Psychology is the scientific study of mental processes and behaviour: how we think, feel, perceive, remember and act. Its scientific character lies in method -- systematic observation and measurement -- rather than in white coats, and its subject matter includes both inner experience and outward action.
concepts.key_idea: A science of the inner and the outer -- mental processes and behaviour studied by systematic method.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy101.txt opening sections (nature and role of psychology, understanding mind and behaviour, psychology as science)
question_patterns: define psychology in terms of mind and behaviour
in class 11 what is psychology: why is psychology called a science
what is the difference between mental processes and behaviour
give examples of behaviour that psychologists study
how does the study of mind differ from common sense about people
explain the term behaviour as used in psychology

solution_steps.explain: Mental processes are inner experiences -- thinking, feeling, remembering; behaviour is observable action.
Claims about either must rest on systematic observation and verifiable evidence.
Understanding mind and behaviour lets psychology improve learning, work, relationships and health.

concepts.title: Growth of the Discipline: From Philosophy to Modern Psychology
concepts.definition: Psychology's questions are ancient but its science is young: born from philosophy and physiology, it grew through schools such as structuralism, functionalism, behaviourism, Gestalt and psychoanalysis into today's cognitive and humanistic approaches, each adding a window on the person.
concepts.key_idea: Old questions, young science -- each historical school added one more window on the mind.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy101.txt growth sections (growth of the discipline, structuralism functionalism behaviourism gestalt psychoanalysis, cognitive and humanistic approaches)
question_patterns: trace the growth of psychology as a discipline
in class 11 what is psychology: how did behaviourism change psychology
what did the psychoanalytic school contribute
what is the cognitive approach in psychology
which schools emphasised the whole and which emphasised parts

solution_steps.explain: Psychology separated from philosophy when it adopted experimental method for mental questions.

Structuralists analysed elements of consciousness; behaviourists demanded observable action; psychoanalysts probed the unconscious; Gestalt stressed wholes; cognitive and humanistic views restored mind and growth.
Contemporary psychology borrows from all windows, studying persons across development, culture and situation.

concepts.title: Fields and Applications of Psychology
concepts.definition: Psychology branches into fields of study and work: cognitive, developmental and social psychology, and applied streams -- clinical and counselling psychology, organisational and educational psychology, sports and health psychology -- each applying the science to human problems in its arena.
concepts.key_idea: One science, many arenas -- from clinic to classroom to playground, psychology applies wherever people act.
concepts.textbook_ref: kepy101.txt fields sections (different fields of psychology, clinical counselling organisational educational sports health psychology, applications)
question_patterns: name the major fields of psychology
in class 11 what is psychology: what does a clinical psychologist do
how is psychology applied in education and organisations
what is the role of a counselling psychologist
match given problems to the fields of psychology that handle them

solution_steps.explain: Cognitive, developmental, social and biological psychology map basic processes across the life span and society.
Clinical and counselling psychology treat distress; organisational, educational, sports and health psychology improve performance and well-being in their settings.
All fields share the scientific study of mind and behaviour, differing mainly in application.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A friend says psychology can read anyone's mind at a glance. Use the definition of psychology as a science to correct him.

solution_template.explain: Psychology infers mental processes from careful evidence, never by intuition at a glance.
Its claims come from systematic observation, experiments and measurement open to checking.
Psychology is a science of mind and behaviour -- disciplined study, not a magic trick.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Sort these problems to the right field: exam anxiety, low factory productivity, a child not speaking yet, an athlete losing focus.

solution_template.explain: Exam anxiety belongs to counselling or clinical psychology.

solution_template.action: assign the organisational and developmental cases
solution_template.explain: Factory productivity goes to organisational psychology; delayed speech to developmental psychology.
A distracted athlete is sports psychology's client -- one science, many arenas.
